title: Interview Playbook
objectives: Run a 45-minute interview in six stages
Close with risks and next steps

cards.title: 45-minute map
cards.body: Six stages: requirements (0–5 min), estimation (5–10), API (10–15), high-level design (15–25), deep dive (25–40), wrap-up (40–45). The same plan runs in Interview mode.

cards.title: Drive the whiteboard
cards.body: Label sync vs async paths, data stores, and queues. Narrate failure modes while you draw—not after.

cards.title: What to cover in each stage
cards.body: Requirements: core flows, scale, exclusions. Estimation: peak QPS, storage, the number that drives the design. API: key endpoints and safe retries. High-level design: the hot path end to end. Deep dive: the riskiest part and its failure modes. Wrap-up: trade-offs, bottlenecks, next steps. These are the same six stages as Lesson 1 and Interview mode.

cards.title: Signals interviewers want
cards.body: Clear scope, realistic math, idempotent writes, observability, and explicit consistency/latency choices.

cards.title: Closing script
cards.body: Summarize bottlenecks, metrics, and what you would prototype in week one.

questions.prompt: Put the Interview Playbook time budget in order.
questions.explanation: The six-stage plan used everywhere in this course: 5 + 5 + 5 + 10 + 15 + 5 = 45 minutes. Adjust if the interviewer steers you.

questions.prompt: The interviewer says “Design BookMyShow.” What is the best first move?

choices.label: Clarify scope: booking flow, scale, hold time
Pick a database for the seats first
Estimate storage for all the movie posters
Draw the microservices you would build

questions.explanation: Requirements come before numbers and boxes.

questions.prompt: Ten minutes are left and you are deep in one component. What should you do?

choices.label: Keep going deeper into that component
Ask the interviewer for more time
Start over with a simpler new design
Step back, cover the rest briefly, state trade-offs

questions.prompt: Which is a signal interviewers want to hear?

choices.label: Working code for the booking endpoint, written out in full
An explicit consistency choice, such as “seat holds need strong consistency”
A list of every AWS service that could possibly be used
A promise that the design never fails under any load

questions.prompt: When should you mention failure modes?

choices.label: Only if asked
Never: it sounds negative
While drawing each component
After the interview
Summarise bottlenecks, metrics and what to build first
Ask the interviewer how you did overall
Re-read all the requirements from the start
Apologise for the gaps you did not cover

flashcards.front: How long does each stage get in a 45-minute interview?
flashcards.back: Requirements 5, estimation 5, API 5, high-level design 10, deep dive 15, wrap-up 5 minutes.

flashcards.front: You reach minute 25 without a complete request path. What do you do?
flashcards.back: Say so, simplify to one read and one write path end to end, then pick the deep dive.

flashcards.front: What goes in a strong wrap-up?
flashcards.back: The main trade-off you chose, what breaks first at 10× scale, what you would monitor, and what you would build first.
